learning_outcomes.text: basic knowledge of probabilities and random variables, and of the analysis of signals and systems in the time and frequency domain.
The student will be able to process deterministic signals in the case of discrete and continuous time, in the time and frequency domain.
The student will be introduced to the analysis of random signals with a specific focus on random variables.
develop their critical judgment in evaluating classmates and collectively discussing topics.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the study of signals: random and deterministic, analogical, sampled, quantized, numerical.
Elementary signals with continuous time and discrete time.
Definition and properties of the Dirac impulse.
Energy and power of a signal.
Operations on signals (translation, reflection, change of scale, scalar product, orthogonality, convolution, correlation).
Basic properties Systems and analysis in the time domain.
Impulsive response of an LTI system.
Systems and analysis in the frequency domain.
Energy Spectral Density (ESD) and Power Spectral Density (PSD) for deterministic signals.
Parseval and Wiener-Khintchine theorems for deterministic signals.
Probability: Axiomatic, classical and frequentistic definition.
Random variables: Discrete random variables, pmf.
Transformations of random variables, Position and scale transformation.
Expectation and moments: Definition and meaning of statistical expectation.
Moments of a random variable, mean square value and variance.
Random vectors: mean, correlation matrix and covariance matrix.
Linear combination of random variables: mean and variance.
Properties of Gaussian vectors, linear combination of Gaussian variables.
Course closing with some insights of most common random processes/signals (Poisson, Bernoulli, Binomial, Cauchy, Uniform, etc.).
assessment_rules: The verification is done with a written test, which can be divided into two parts. Intracourse, non-mandatory tests are also provided for both parts to encourage continuous study. The test is considered passed if the total score is 18/30 or higher. The proposed final grade is based on the arithmetic mean of the scores achieved in the individual tests.
